- When sentiment is strongly positive (≥ 0.7) and forecast shows a sharp upward spike, reduce the peak by 5–10% to avoid overshoot.  
- If sentiment turns negative (≤ 0.3) and forecast is trending up, adjust downward by 3–7% to reflect mean reversion.  
- For 30-day forecasts, if the last 3–5 days of history show a clear downward trend, reduce forecasted mean by 2–5% to account for lagged momentum.  
- When sentiment is volatile (alternating ±0.3–0.6) and forecast is erratic, smooth out extremes by averaging adjacent forecast points.  
- If true outcome consistently underperforms forecast in early days (1–7), apply a 3–5% downward bias to future forecasts.  
- For sentiment history with high positive peaks followed by low sentiment, expect a 2–4% downward correction in the next 7–14 days.
